name: Matte PLA
chemical_makeup: PLA compounded with a fine, non-abrasive mineral/particulate matting agent that scatters light at the surface; a surface-effect filler package rather than a reinforcing fibre (Polymaker PolyTerra uses a comparable plant-fibre-derived matting approach)
summary: Base PLA plus a light matting filler that kills gloss and visually hides layer lines and fingerprints. Versus base PLA it is denser (1.31 vs 1.24 g/cm³), runs 5-10 °C hotter and 10-20 % slower because the filler raises melt viscosity, and is somewhat weaker and more brittle (tensile XY 30 MPa vs 45-65 MPa) — everything else, including drying and warp behaviour, is base-PLA-equivalent.

printing.notes: Delta vs base PLA: same nominal 190-230 °C window but Bambu tests specimens at 220 °C and community guidance is +5 to +10 °C over plain PLA, with a 10-20 % speed reduction from your usual PLA profile because the matting filler raises melt viscosity. Bambu's TDS still rates the material to 300 mm/s on capable hardware. The filler load is low and mineral (not glass or carbon), so a brass nozzle is fine — this is the key hardware difference from pla-wood, pla-glow and pla-metal.

feeding.notes: Rigid and non-abrasive; feeds through Bowden or direct drive identically to base PLA and is listed AMS-compatible in Bambu's material table with no caveats. The most AMS-safe of the six aesthetic PLA variants alongside pla-gradient. No feeding assistant needed.

drying.dryness_validation: No popping or steam at the nozzle and no stringing on a retraction test; note that the matte surface hides the fine bubbling that betrays wet silk PLA, so judge by sound and stringing rather than by finish
drying.notes: Essentially unchanged from base PLA — Bambu specifies 50 °C for 8 h. The mineral filler is not meaningfully hygroscopic, so this is not a moisture-critical material the way pla-wood is.

storage.recommendations: Sealed bag or drybox with desiccant between uses; tolerates open-air storage about as well as base PLA

price.notes: Bambu PLA Matte around $19.99-22.99/kg. The premium over base PLA has narrowed to marginal in recent years — cheaper than pla-gradient, pla-wood, pla-glow and pla-metal, which sit near $25/kg

recommended: parts where layer lines and fingerprints must not read
not_recommended: snap-fit and clip geometry (more brittle than base PLA)
sustained-load or outdoor parts, same as base PLA

properties.notes: Bambu PLA Matte TDS: density 1.31 g/cm³ (the densest of the unfilled-looking PLA variants, and above base PLA's 1.24), tensile XY 30±5 MPa and Z 22±4 MPa, elongation XY 14.8±4.2 % and Z 4.8±1.7 %, Tg 61 °C, HDT 58 °C at 0.45 MPa and 52 °C at 1.8 MPa. Elongation is far better than pla-silk's 2.8 %, so 'more brittle than base PLA' is a relative statement: matte is the toughest of the aesthetic variants after pla-gradient. Flexural strength is reported lower than base PLA because filler particles act as stress concentrators, but no primary datasheet figure was found.

compatibility.notes: Standard PLA-family behaviour, identical to the base entry: welds to itself and other PLA grades, releases cleanly from PETG. Matte and base PLA are frequently combined in multi-colour prints with no interface penalty beyond the slight strength drop of the matte side.

plate_recommendations.notes: The best aesthetic pairing of the six variants: a textured first layer matches the matte top surfaces so the whole part reads uniformly non-reflective. Smooth PEI also works. This is the opposite of pla-silk, where texture degrades the finish.

emissions.notes: No difference from base PLA reported; the mineral matting agent is inert at printing temperature and produces no unusual odour, unlike pla-wood's charring fibre.

safety_notes: The matting filler package is not food-contact certified; treat matte parts as decorative.
additional_notes: Matte finish is a filler effect, not a process effect — unlike pla-silk gloss, it cannot be tuned in or out with temperature and speed.

provenance.conflicts: Tensile strength: Bambu's TDS gives 30±5 MPa XY, while a secondary comparison source cites 40-60 MPa for matte against 50-70 MPa for standard PLA — the sources agree on the direction (matte is weaker than base PLA) but not the magnitude; the manufacturer datasheet is recorded. Flexural strength is cited by a secondary source at 50-80 MPa vs 70-90 MPa for base PLA, unverified against any datasheet. Speed: Bambu rates 300 mm/s while community guidance says run 10-20 % slower than base PLA; both are captured in the printing range and notes.
